While the Ministry of Health confirmed no systemic national drug shortages, the attack highlights escalating strikes on logistics following drone hits on schools and warehouses across the capital.

Russian Drones Breach Moldovan Airspace, Crash in 4 Districts — Russian strike drones violated Moldovan airspace during an attack on Ukraine on Saturday, Oct. 3, detonating and scattering debris across the Căușeni, Ștefan Vodă, Hîncești, and Anenii Noi districts. The vote takes place under heightened border anxiety and Russian drone incursions, with Kulbergs pledging to maintain 5% GDP defense spending.

Drones Strike Russian Tsymbulovo Jet-UAV Base in Oryol — Ukrainian strike drones hit the Tsymbulovo droneport in Russia’s Oryol region early Saturday morning, Oct. 3, sparking multiple fires across storage and launch sites for jet-powered Geran drones, according to satellite monitoring. The facility, which underwent rapid expansion in September, serves as Moscow’s primary launch base for turbojet drone waves targeting Kyiv.

Russian Drill Simulates Incursion, ‘Security Zone’ in Tsentr-2026 Games — Russian forces practiced transitioning to an offensive and creating a “security zone” inside the territory of a neighboring state during the strategic Tsentr-2026 exercises in the Central Asian direction, according to Kremlin reports. Analysts noted Kazakhstan fits the profile of the simulated adversary as over 47,000 troops conducted maneuvers integrating tactical lessons from the war in Ukraine.

Ukraine Denies Reports Western Embassies Plan Kyiv Relocation — The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine (MFA) has refuted reports that Western embassies are drawing up contingency plans to relocate diplomatic personnel from Kyiv to Lviv or eastern Poland. Spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi emphasized that standard protocols mandate prior notification and confirmed that no foreign missions have submitted relocation requests, responding to claims in The Guardian as Russia intensifies infrastructure st

Russia Orders Surge in European Hybrid Attacks — The Main Directorate of Intelligence of Ukraine (HUR) warned that the Kremlin has instructed the GRU and FSB to escalate hybrid operations and sabotage across EU and NATO nations, specifically targeting military sites, infrastructure, and Starlink ground stations. The alert follows a suspected arson attack against a Starlink facility in Poland and foiled sabotage at Leipzig Airport.

Ukrainian Mirage 2000 Downs Russian Cruise Missile With Cannon — A Ukrainian Air Force Mirage 2000-5F fighter jet intercepted and shot down a Russian S8000 Banderol compact cruise missile using its onboard 30mm DEFA 554 cannon, marking the first confirmed gun kill of the turbojet-powered munition by the French-supplied jet.

Russian Jet Drone Strikes Kyiv’s North Bridge, Injures 2 — A Russian jet-powered strike drone hit Kyiv’s North Bridge on Saturday morning, Oct. 3, damaging the road surface and overhead trolleybus lines and forcing the closure of westbound traffic across the Dnipro River, as well as injuring two people. The strike compounds mounting transit disruption following earlier attacks that shut the South Bridge, alongside overnight ballistic strikes that killed one person.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 2, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 2, 2026.

Russian Ballistic Missiles and Drones Hit Kyiv, Killing 1 — Kyiv came under another combined Russian ballistic missile and drone attack early Saturday, with one person killed, two wounded and fires reported in several districts.

Stubb: Every Russian Threat Should Bring More Support for Ukraine — Finnish President Alexander Stubb said Russia’s hybrid pressure on Europe should result in more support for Ukraine, while Maia Sandu and Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Moscow’s threat extends well beyond the current war.

Sandu: Russia Will Remain Major Threat to Europe Even After Ukraine War Ends — Maia Sandu warned that Russia’s threat to Europe will persist beyond the war in Ukraine, calling for stronger European defenses, accountability and faster EU enlargement.

Ukraine Records Nearly 227,000 Russian War Crimes Since Full-Scale Invasion — Ukraine’s National Police has opened nearly 244,000 criminal proceedings linked to Russia’s invasion, including 226,766 war crimes cases and 153 involving sexual violence.

Russian Drone Strikes Fire-Rescue Unit in Zaporizhzhia Region, Wounding Rescuer — Ukraine’s emergency service said Russian forces deliberately targeted a fire-rescue unit in Zaporizhzhia region, injuring one rescuer.

Russia Plans Record $200B Defense Budget as Healthcare, Education, Face Cuts — Russia’s 2027 draft budget includes a sharp increase in military spending while reducing planned healthcare, education and social expenditures, highlighting the growing fiscal cost of the war.

Putin Ally Schröder Takes Russian Business Post After Kremlin Floated Him as Ukraine Mediator — Gerhard Schröder has joined the supervisory board of Russian retailer Hyperglobus, deepening his ties to Moscow after the Kremlin repeatedly presented him as a potential mediator over Ukraine.

Zelensky: Putin’s Goal Is Not Donbas but All of Ukraine — Volodymyr Zelensky said Vladimir Putin’s latest rhetoric shows Moscow’s ambitions extend beyond Donbas to all of Ukraine and warned that Russia also seeks renewed influence over neighboring states.

Poland Drafts ‘Pre-War’ Readiness Law to Speed Up Allied Troop Deployment — Poland’s Defense Ministry is drafting a law to prepare the state for a heightened readiness phase before martial law is declared, Polish media reported on Friday, Oct. 2. The bill would essentially allow earlier deployment of Polish and allied troops and address hybrid, cyber and disinformation threats.

41 Ukrainians Return From Russian Occupation via Volyn, Including 9 children — Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets said on Friday, Oct. 2 that 41 Ukrainians – including four children and five teenagers – returned from Russian occupation via Volyn in August and September. He warned that civilians in occupied Oleshky in the Kherson region still face extreme difficulty leaving, essentially describing the city as a “death trap.”

Ukraine to Speed Up Identification of Fallen Soldiers as Over 26,000 Bodies Returned — Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov announced on Friday, Oct. 2 that Ukraine will create an interagency group to speed up identification of fallen soldiers. More than 26,000 bodies and remains have been repatriated, however, a significant share remain unidentified as the process sometimes takes up to several years. According to Ukrainian police, many of the bodies arrive with explosive devices hidde

Putin’s Pantsir Problem: Why Russia’s Air Defense Is Failing — In this episode of Point of Impact, former U.S. Navy SEAL Chuck Pfarrer breaks down why Putin’s flagship short-range air defense system is fundamentally flawed.

G7 Members Agree to Release Up to 100M Barrels of Oil Reserves to Curb Fuel Prices — G7 countries agreed on Oct 2. to release up to 100 million barrels of oil and diesel reserves over four months, following weeks of pressure from the US. The deal rules out export bans among members, French President Emmanual Macron said, while US President Donald Trump previously pinned the blame on Ukraine’s refinery strikes on Russia for soaring diesel prices.

Zelensky Orders Housing Support Options for Teachers Ahead of Education Workers’ Day — President Volodymyr Zelensky visited a school on Friday, Oct. 2 ahead of the Education Workers’ Day. Subsequently, he ordered authorities to work out options for additional housing and financial support for teachers, including through the “eOselia” mortgage program. The visit came just a day after Russia targeted a school in Kyiv with a drone carrying a 50 kilogram (110 lbs) warhead.

Chisinau Airport Evacuated Over Bomb Threat — Chisinau International Airport suspended passenger check-in and evacuated its terminal following a bomb threat on Friday. Moldovan authorities warned that scheduled flights could be delayed or changed while security teams inspected the airport.

Russian Drones Hit Kyiv’s South Bridge Again as Traffic Collapses — Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said at 5:50 p.m. on Friday that Russian forces struck Kyiv’s South Bridge again, after multiple strikes the day before shut down the bridges and paralyzed traffic in the Ukrainian capital. Zelensky said Friday that Vladimir Putin had ordered his troops to remove restraints on hitting civilian targets to pressure Kyiv toward capitulation.

Ukraine Could Become Europe’s Storage Hub for US Gas — An Atlantic Council analysis proposes using Ukraine’s underground storage network to distribute US gas across European markets. Existing import agreements provide a foundation, but expansion would depend on investment, infrastructure connections and security.

‘We Can No Longer Pretend’: Kyiv Faces Fight for Survival, Klitschko Warns — Klitschko warned that Kyiv’s functioning increasingly depends on safety and survival as Russian attacks damage infrastructure. Metro services across the Southern Bridge during yellow-level alerts await an expert assessment.

Kyiv Metro Awaits Safety Clearance to Resume South Bridge Crossings — Kyiv’s metro is ready to resume Green Line service across the South Bridge during yellow air alerts, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Trains can cross again only after experts confirm the bridge is safe following repeated Russian drone strikes.

Ukrainian Grandmother Detained in Alleged FSB Trap — Kazakhstan detained Ukrainian citizen Liubov Rozhanska at Astana airport after she arrived to collect her grandson, whom a Ukrainian court had ordered to live with his father in Odesa. Russia accuses her of attempting to abduct the child, while her lawyer alleges the proposed handover was a planned FSB provocation.

Ukrainian Startup Osavul Raises $10 Million to Expand Threat Detection — Ukrainian-founded Osavul has raised $10 million in a funding round led by 33N Ventures. The Luxembourg-headquartered company plans to expand its threat intelligence platform to businesses and critical infrastructure operators while continuing its work with government and defense clients.

Ukraine Denies F-16 Crisis Over Maintenance and Parts — Ukraine has rejected reports that maintenance delays and parts shortages have grounded more than half its F-16 fleet, saying it can keep the US-made jets operational through winter despite demanding conditions and challenges sourcing components.

Ukraine Tests Five High-Speed Drone Interceptor Models to Counter Russia’s Jet-Powered Attacks — Ukraine is testing five high-speed interceptor drone models to counter Russia’s increasingly common jet-powered attack drones, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. One model could reach production of around 400 units by the end of October as Kyiv races to strengthen its air defenses.

Kremlin Urges US-Russia Deals Before Ukraine Settlement — The Kremlin said Russia and the US could begin mutually beneficial economic projects before reaching a settlement in Ukraine. The comments followed Putin envoy Dmitriev’s Washington talks with US officials on ending the war and potential postwar energy cooperation.

Russia Wants to Force Kyiv Residents Out of Capital, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia is targeting Kyiv’s civilian infrastructure and schools to pressure residents into leaving the capital. Mayor Vitali Klitschko warned that the city is facing a “very dramatic situation” as Russian strikes hit critical infrastructure, housing, logistics and energy facilities.

Russia Lost Ground Despite Putin’s Claims of Major Advances, ISW Says — ISW estimates that Russia has suffered a net loss of controlled territory since March. A separate measure that includes infiltration zones shows limited gains. Its September mapping also records Russian losses, although some Ukrainian advances occurred in earlier months.

Russia Plans to Cut 90% of Power, Heat and Water in Ukraine’s Biggest Cities — Russia aims to cripple electricity, heating and water supplies in Kyiv, Kharkiv, and Odesa this winter, according to an alleged intercepted plan described by The New York Times. The newspaper obtained a copy but could not independently authenticate it.

SBU Nabs 2 Zaporizhzhia Teenagers Accused of Moscow-Backed Assassination Plot — The counterintelligence unit of Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU) said on Friday that the police had detained two teenagers plotting to attack four Ukrainian servicemen. It said the men were acting on behalf of Russia’s FSB after being recruited through social media.

‘No Rules Now’: Putin Orders Civilian Attacks, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky told the Financial Times that intercepted communications indicated Vladimir Putin had ordered Russia’s military to abandon previous constraints and intensify attacks on civilian sites. Kyiv says the shift coincides with a surge in jet-powered drone strikes on schools, hospitals, telecommunications infrastructure and data centers.

No EU Membership for Ukraine on Jan. 1, 2027, Brussels Admits — EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos has ruled out Ukraine joining on Jan. 1, 2027. Civil society’s September assessment puts implementation of its priority reform plan at just 15%, while Ukrainian diplomatic reporting had already questioned whether even symbolic political membership next year was achievable.

Kyiv Grinds to a Halt as Russian Strikes Shut Bridges, Force People to Walk — Kyiv was hit by major traffic disruption on Friday after Russian strikes forced the closure or restriction of several bridges across the Dnipro River. Massive jams left public transport delayed, taxi fares soaring, and some commuters abandoning vehicles and crossing the city on foot.

Last-Minute Push for Russia Sanctions Bill — Ukrainian advocates mounted a last-minute lobbying push on Capitol Hill, working to sway undecided lawmakers and build support for the Russia sanctions bill, which ultimately passed the House 262-159.

Latvia Detains Couple Suspected of Spying for Russia — Latvia has detained two citizens suspected of spying for Russia’s GRU, allegedly collecting information on defense systems, NATO activities, Ukraine support, military aircraft and a key NATO base. Authorities say one suspect photographed Ādaži Military Base by private aircraft. Searches uncovered electronic devices and documents as the investigation into potential espionage and sabotage support continues.

South Korea Warns ‘Further Measures’ if Ukraine Refuses Public Apology — South Korea has warned of “further measures” if Ukraine does not apologize for revealing the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul, escalating a diplomatic dispute over the POWs’ safety and the confidentiality of their handover.

646 Drones Swarm Russia as Fires Hit Europe’s Largest Tank Farm, Oil Facilities — Fires were reported near a major oil refinery and chemical plant in Volgograd and at a large oil storage facility in Samara following a massive overnight drone attack. Russia claimed its air defenses intercepted 646 drones across 14 regions.

Russian Strike on European Arms Factory Would Trigger Article 5, EU Defense Chief Says — EU Defence Commissioner said a Russian strike on a weapons factory in a NATO country could trigger Article 5. Officials also warned of Russian hybrid attacks and nuclear rhetoric while saying Moscow currently lacks the capacity to invade NATO.

Russian Attack Kills 1 in Kyiv High-Rise, Shuts Down Bridges Across the Capital — A Russian attack killed one person and damaged a 25-story residential building in Kyiv. Strikes also disrupted traffic across three major bridges as Ukrainian air defenses intercepted or suppressed 88 of 108 drones launched overnight.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 1, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 1, 2026.

Russia Turns Its Drone War on Kyiv’s Dnipro Bridges – Why Now? — Repeated Russian drone strikes on Kyiv’s Southern Bridge mark a notable escalation against the capital’s transport infrastructure, disrupting metro and road traffic while raising questions over Moscow’s changing target priorities.

US Announces $24.4 Billion Contract to Speed Up Missile Production — The Pentagon awarded Raytheon a $24.4 billion contract to accelerate SM-6 production as US officials confront depleted missile inventories and the possibility of renewed strikes on Iran.

CCTV Captures Russian Drone Slamming Into Kyiv School With 104 Children Inside – Warhead Fails to Detonate — CTV captured the moment a Russian drone struck a Kyiv school with 104 children and 60 staff inside. All survived after taking shelter underground, while the drone’s warhead failed to detonate.

Russian Military Helicopter Crash Kills 3 in Voronezh Region — A Russian military helicopter crashed in the Anninsky district of Voronezh region, killing all three people on board, according to Russian and independent media reports.

If Moscow Is Not Stopped in Ukraine, NATO Itself Could Be Next, Merz Warns — Merz warned that weakening German support could destabilize Europe and Ukraine, arguing European unity and military strength are essential to securing peace.

New Russian Mobilization Could Leave Low-Skill Workers Poorer, KSE Institute Says — KSE Institute finds that sign-on bonuses for Russian contract soldiers now total around RUB 1 trillion annually, while the wage gains from labor scarcity under mobilization scenarios would amount to only RUB 20–200 billion. A call-up of 500,000 could add 0.1–0.2 percentage points to real wage growth, and one million 0.6–1.2 points.

Ukraine, EU Say 2026 Defense Needs Covered as Kyiv Starts Freezing Allocations — The European Commission and Ukraine both said they have identified the means to cover Ukraine’s 2026 budget and defense needs and agreed to move ahead with €45 billion ($50.6 billion) of the Ukraine Support Loan for 2027. Meanwhile, Kyiv has started freezing non-priority budget allocations from October, as external aid fell behind plan. According to Finance Minister Serhiy Marchenko, a $32.6 billion gap remains for

Russian Strike on European Arms Factory Would Trigger Article 5, EU’s Kubilius Says — EU Defense Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said on Thursday, Oct. 1 that a Russian strike on a weapons factory in Europe would trigger NATO’s Article 5. His remarks followed Moscow’s earlier warning that European factories producing arms for Ukraine could be possible military targets.

Russian Drone Hits Kyiv’s Southern Bridge for Third Time in One Day, Damaging Support — A third Russian drone hit Kyiv’s Southern Bridge on Thursday after two earlier strikes near its supports, damaging the roadway and metro infrastructure.

‘A Deliberate Tactic’: Zelensky Condemns Russian Drone Strike on Kyiv School — A Russian drone struck a school in Kyiv on Thursday, Oct. 1, while more than 100 children and over 60 teachers sheltered inside. President Volodymyr Zelensky called strikes on schools a deliberate Russian tactic, while Ukrainian authorities separately said that the drone’s warhead failed to detonate.

Putin Raises Nuclear Threat Over Kaliningrad, Says Russia Monitors Arms Factories in Europe — Speaking at the Valdai Club on Thursday, Oct. 1, Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed that a “direct attack” on Russia or Kaliningrad would raise the question of using all its weapons, even nuclear. The warning follows Moscow’s message to NATO this week, threatening its “entire arsenal” over the exclave.

UK Announces Package of 31 Sanctions Against Russia — The UK government has unveiled a package of 31 new sanctions against Russia, targeting its LNG shadow fleet and global disinformation networks. The strict measures also penalize individuals responsible for the torture of Ukrainian civilians and the forced deportation of children.

Ukraine Reports First Combat Use of Domestically Produced FP-7 Ballistic Missile — Ukraine had used its domestically produced FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time on Thursday, Oct. 1, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, marking a milestone in Kyiv’s push to build its own strike weapons as Russia intensifies its campaign on civilian infrastructure nationwide.

Sledgehammer for Putin — Congress has handed President Trump a sweeping sanctions bill, signed Sept. 18, that lets him hit Russia's oil, banks, and buyers like China and India by Oct. 18 unless Moscow agrees to peace talks. The author argues Trump must abandon his "personal diplomacy" with Putin and use the leverage, as Russia's economy weakens and public pressure mounts.

PACE Declares Russia’s New State Duma Illegitimate — The Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) adopted a new resolution on Wednesday, Sept. 30, declaring Russia’s new State Duma illegitimate following the Sept. 18-20 vote held in Russia and occupied territories of Ukraine. During the meeting, PACE urged sanctions on election organizers and further limits on tourist visas for Russian nationals.

‘Never Hurts to Have Their Name on Things’ – Drone Startup Linked to Trump’s Sons — A fledgling defense enterprise, Powerus, has said it plans to import Ukrainian and other foreign technology to help meet rising Pentagon demand. Its CEO said it was planning to issue an IPO this month after it merges with a company part-owned by Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump.

Ukrainian Air Force MiG-29 Pilot Killed in Combat — Ukraine’s Air Force Command reported via Facebook that a Ukrainian pilot from the 40th “Ghost of Kyiv” Tactical Aviation Brigade was killed during combat Thursday, Oct. 1. The pilot, Capt. Marat Mambetov, was a flight leader within the brigade.

20-Year-Old Sentenced to Life for Killing Ukrainian Nationalist Diehard — A court in Lviv sentenced Viacheslav Zinchenko to life imprisonment for the July 2024 murder of a prominet Ukrainian nationalist figure and  former lawmaker, Iryna Farion. Zinchenko denied the charges, but the court found him guilty based on forensic examinations, surveillance footage, digital records and evidence of preparations for the attack.

Trump Offers Russia Sanctions Relief Using His Belarusian Model — Recent US prisoner negotiations with Belarus and Russia reveal a broader strategy in which humanitarian releases can pave the way for sanctions relief and economic cooperation. Gerashchenko argues that Moscow could potentially exploit this approach to secure relief from Washington while avoiding concessions on Ukraine.

Ukraine Rejects Australia’s Ageing Tiger Helicopters — Ukraine has withdrawn its request for Australia’s retiring Eurocopter Tiger attack helicopters after assessing their maintenance costs, technical condition and spare-parts requirements. Kyiv is instead cautiously exploring US-made Apache helicopters and other platforms to modernize its army aviation fleet in face of formidable Russian air defenses.

Sweden Ready to Take the Fight Into Russia if NATO Attacked — On Monday, Colonel Karl Bergqvist, head of Sweden’s Air Warfare Center, said that if attacked by Moscow, Sweden would target sites deep inside Russia. He said that the air force currently had the weapons to carry this out and was in the process of acquiring even larger long-range weapons.

Russia Can Still Finance Its War, but Costs and Risks Are Rising, KSE Institute Says — KSE Institute finds that Russia’s federal budget deficit reached RUB 5.8 trillion in January–August 2026, 48% higher year-on-year and 20% above the revised full-year target, while liquid NWF assets are down around 60% from February 2022. Domestic borrowing remains the main financing source, but it is becoming more costly and increasingly dependent on bank capacity and CBR liquidity.

Kyiv Reshapes Responses to Russian Strikes — Zelensky said Ukraine has adjusted its response system to Russian attacks on Kyiv’s critical infrastructure. He also ordered an urgent review of air defense and F-16 ammunition supplies, faster deliveries, and stronger resilience measures across regions and major cities.

Media Report Assassination Attempt on Fire Point Co-Owner – ‘Somewhat Exaggerated,’ He Says — Israeli journalist Sergei Auslander reported an alleged assassination attempt on Fire Point co-owner Denys Shtilierman near Kyiv, citing an unnamed source. Shtilierman responded that reports of his or his guards’ deaths were “somewhat exaggerated,” without directly confirming or denying that an attack occurred.

Accused War Criminal, Ukraine Invasion Commanders Take Up Seats in Russian Duma — War-crimes suspect Nursultan Mussagaleev and 45 other Russia-Ukraine war veterans, including Golovin, Borodai, Brovko, Kuular, Kukensova and Golovchenko, now sit in the State Duma as United Russia deputies after the September 2026 election.

Russia Strikes Kyiv Nuclear Institute Housing Reactor — A Russian drone struck the grounds of Kyiv’s Institute for Nuclear Research, which houses the VVR-M research reactor, Ukraine’s nuclear regulator said. A resulting fire was extinguished, while the reactor and its safety systems were not damaged. No casualties or changes in radiation levels were reported.

UAE Government Used Sanctioned Russian ‘Shadow’ Airline — A Defense News investigation into the activities of Aviacon Zitotrans, a Russian air cargo company sanctioned because of links to Moscow’s mercenary forces, found it had been used extensively by the UAE government over the last year or so.

WATCH: Ukraine Hits Black Sea Target and Russian Drone Site — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine struck an unspecified target in the Black Sea, a drone launch and storage site in Russia’s Oryol region, an oil facility in Samara, and a military supply depot in Bryansk. He did not disclose what was hit at sea or provide details about the damage.

46,230 Russian Troop Losses in September, Moscow Prepares 120,000 New Conscripts — Ukraine’s General Staff reported a record 46,230 Russian troop losses in September, bringing the 2026 total to 326,900. Meanwhile, Russia plans to send about 120,000 conscripts to military units this autumn, officials said.

Two Drone Strikes Hit Kyiv’s South Bridge, Metro and Surface Traffic Suspended — Two drone strikes hit the area near the supports of Kyiv’s South Bridge, prompting authorities to suspend metro and surface transport. Municipal specialists are inspecting the structure, while unverified footage circulating online reportedly shows fires and drone debris.

Bulgarian PM Warns Putin Holds a ‘Nuclear Trump Card’ — Responding to Russian threats to use nuclear weapons in defense of Kaliningrad, Mark Rutte condemned Moscow’s rhetoric and said NATO would remain undeterred. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev took a different view, warning that President Vladimir Putin retains a “nuclear trump card” and calling for increased diplomatic efforts to reduce the risk of escalation.

Kremlin Critic Kasparov Says US Intelligence Warned Life ‘In Danger’ — Kasparov said US and Lithuanian security services warned him and ally Ivan Tyutrin that their lives were in danger. The warnings came after US authorities charged five alleged Russian intelligence agents over plots targeting Kremlin critics abroad.

Trump Leaves Key US Allies Out of NATO Group Meeting — The Trump administration excluded the UK, France and the Baltic states from an October meeting of a select NATO working group in Poland, Politico reported. The Bergen Group includes six European allies favored by the Pentagon, raising concerns that Washington is dividing NATO members into “good” and “bad” camps.

Ukraine Marks Defenders’ Day as Zelensky Honors Warriors From the Lyman Front — Ukraine marks the Day of Defenders on Thursday, Oct. 1, honoring the men and women protecting the country. Zelensky delivered his address from the Lyman front, paying tribute to fallen heroes and thanking those defending Ukraine’s independence.

'Watering the Desert': EU Pushes Back as Ukraine Seeks More Money Despite €90B Aid Package — Brussels is resisting Ukraine’s push for additional funding, saying Kyiv must first implement reforms and unlock money already approved under the €90 billion EU loan. The dispute has also revived divisions over whether frozen Russian assets can finance Ukraine’s needs.

Russian Drone Strikes Kyiv School as Children Shelter During Morning Attack — A Russian drone struck a school in Kyiv’s Solomianskyi district on Thursday, sparking a fire while children were sheltering. A second strike hit warehouse facilities nearby. No casualties had been reported at the time of publication.

Russian Radicals Baptize Moon to ‘Make it Orthodox’ — ussian ultranationalists and Putin-linked bikers held a ceremony near the Estonian border to “baptize” the Moon and link it to Russia. The ritual involved a Bronze Age petroglyph-covered stone that organizers claimed originated in space.

Trump Again Blames Ukraine for Rising US Diesel Prices, Dismissing Middle East War Impact — Trump again blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for soaring US diesel prices, rejecting the Middle East war as the main cause. His energy secretary acknowledged disruptions from the Middle East and China also contributed to tighter diesel supplies.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 30, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 30, 2026.

Lockheed Martin in ‘Deep’ Overseas Patriot Production Talks as Ukraine Eyes Domestic Output — Lockheed Martin is in advanced talks over PAC-3 production outside the US as demand triples, while expanding autonomous helicopters, a microwave “drone killer,” and a lower-cost interceptor.

Russia Strikes Odesa Infrastructure Again After Days of Deadly Attacks — Russia struck Odesa infrastructure again after days of attacks that killed civilians and damaged residential, commercial and logistics sites.

Russian Attacks on Kyiv Continue Into Thursday as Drone Crashes Near Playground and Fires Erupt — Russia’s attack on Kyiv continued into early Thursday, injuring a man and causing new fires after Wednesday’s strikes killed three people and wounded seven.

US Extends Waiver for Russian-Controlled Serbian Oil Firm as Exit Talks Drag On — Washington extended NIS’s operating license through Oct. 30 as talks continue over a sale of Russia’s majority stake to Hungary’s MOL.

Lithuania Moves to Ban Russian, Belarusian Artists Who Performed in Occupied Ukraine — Lithuania’s government approved a proposal on Wednesday, Sept. 30 to bar Russian and Belarusian artists who worked in occupied Ukrainian territories or supported Russia’s war from performing in the country. To work in Lithuania, they would have to sign a public declaration condemning Russia’s aggression – a step that could expose them to prosecution at home.
